title: Translational Psychiatry: Evaluating the Monoamine vs. Neurogenic Hypotheses of Depression
description: Contrast classic monoaminergic pharmacotherapy with fast-acting glutamatergic ketamine protocols for treatment-resistant depression.
problemStatement:
A clinical neuropsychiatrist evaluates a 35-year-old patient suffering from severe Treatment-Resistant Depression (TRD) who has failed three distinct courses of SSRIs.

### Your Mission:
1. **Theoretical Failure**: Explain why the therapeutic delay of SSRIs and high non-response rates (~30-40%) undermine the classical monoamine deficiency model.
2. **The BDNF / Synaptogenesis Model**: Describe how chronic stress downregulates Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) and causes loss of dendritic spines in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex.
3. **Ketamine Mechanism**: Explain the cellular mechanism of low-dose sub-anesthetic intravenous Ketamine (an NMDA receptor antagonist): how does blocking NMDA receptors on GABAergic interneurons trigger a glutamate surge, AMPA receptor activation, and mTOR-dependent synaptogenesis within 2 to 24 hours?
hints: Hint 1: Chronic antidepressant administration requires gene expression changes and neurogenesis to produce behavioral improvement.
Hint 2: Ketamine disinhibits pyramidal neurons by blocking NMDA receptors on inhibitory interneurons, sparking rapid spine regrowth.
